newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Chinese vice-premier to leave Israel day early.
newsitem.headline: Chinese vice-premier to leave Israel day early.

text.p: Chinese Vice-Premier Li Lanqing kept to his Jerusalem hotel on Thursday, cancelling all apppointments except for a meeting with Israel's prime minister following the death of China's leader Deng Xiaoping.

Israeli foreign ministry spokesman Ygal Palmor told Reuters Li would leave Israel later on Thursday after meeting Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in the afternoon. Li had originally been set to leave Israel on Friday.
"He has a meeting with Netanyahu at four o'clock (1400 gmt) and he is going back to Beijing tonight," Palmor said.

After a dinner in Tel Aviv on Wednesday night, Li returned to his Jerusalem hotel by a back entrance to avoid journalists staking out the area. Journalists continued waiting outside the hotel on Thursday.
Palmor said Li had been scheduled to visit Israel's Dead Sea Works and diamond bourse on Thursday but cancelled the visits after news of Deng's death on Wednesday.
